title: The SCUT Trial: Masterclass in Steroids for Corneal Ulcers
summary: The Steroids for Corneal Ulcers Trial (SCUT) was a landmark NEI-funded, double-masked, randomized controlled trial that fundamentally changed our approach to adjuvant topical corticosteroids in bacterial keratitis. It proved that while steroids don't benefit everyone, specific subgroups gain significant visual recovery.

sections.title: The SCUT Treatment Protocol
content: Step 1: Corneal Scraping for Gram/Giemsa stain and Culture.
Step 2: Start Moxifloxacin 0.5% (vigamox) every 1 hour (daytime) for 48 hours.
Step 3: Randomize at 48 hours (if non-fungal) to Prednisolone 1% or Placebo.
Step 4: Steroid Dosing: QID x 1 week, then BID x 1 week, then QD x 1 week.
Step 5: Continue Moxifloxacin until re-epithelialization is complete.

sections.title: The Nocardia Warning
content: Nocardia species showed WORSE outcomes with steroids.
Increased scar size at 3 months in steroid group.
Steroids may inhibit the neutrophilic response required to clear Nocardia.
Clinical Tip: Look for 'ginger-root' or 'wreath-like' infiltrates and perform modified acid-fast stain.

sections.title: Primary Result: 3-Month BSCVA
sections.content: Overall, there was NO statistically significant difference in the primary outcome of Best Spectacle-Corrected Visual Acuity (BSCVA) at 3 months between the steroid group and the placebo group. (Mean difference of 0.04 LogMAR; P=0.21). However, significant benefits were discovered in pre-specified subgroup analyses.

sections.title: Key Subgroup Benefits
content: Severe Ulcers: Patients with baseline vision <20/400 (LogMAR >1.3) gained 1.7 lines more vision with steroids.
Central Ulcers: Ulcers covering the central 4mm zone showed improved visual outcomes.
Deep Ulcers: Ulcers with >50% stromal depth at baseline benefited significantly.
Non-Nocardia: When Nocardia was excluded, the steroid group was significantly better than placebo.

content.explanation: Wait 48 hours, Antibiotics first, Identify organism (Exclude Fungal/Nocardia), Timing matters (Early is better), Center/Central ulcers benefit most.

sections.title: Timing of Steroid Initiation
content: Early Steroids (within 2-3 days of antibiotics) resulted in 1-line better vision than late initiation.
Delaying steroids to day 4 or later negated the visual recovery benefit found in the trial.
Conclusion: Start early once the organism is confirmed and fungal/Nocardia is ruled out.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls (Landmark Findings)
content: No increased risk of perforation: Topical steroids did not cause more corneal melting in bacterial ulcers compared to placebo.
Steroids do not delay healing: Re-epithelialization time was equivalent between groups.
Long-term stability: The 12-month follow-up data mirrored the 3-month data, showing visual gains were stable.
Moxifloxacin coverage: 0.5% Moxifloxacin was effective as monotherapy against most bacterial isolates in the trial.
Practice Change: SCUT validated the 'Wait 48 Hours' rule for starting steroids in bacterial keratitis.

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: 1. Suspected Bacterial Ulcer -> Scrape + Culture.
2. Start Fluoroquinolone or Fortifieds Q1H.
3. Review at 48 Hours: Is culture positive for bacteria?
4. If NO FUNGUS or NOCARDIA -> Add Prednisolone 1% QID.
5. Taper steroids over 3 weeks while monitoring IOP and epithelial closure.

sections.title: Secondary Analysis: The 12-Month Data
sections.content: Follow-up at 12 months confirmed that the visual benefits seen at 3 months (especially in the low baseline vision group) persisted. There was no evidence that steroids led to delayed complications or recurrences in the long term.

content.explanation: Topical steroids are SAFE in bacterial ulcers once fungal/Nocardia are excluded. They improve visual outcomes in SEVERE ulcers (worse than 20/400) and CENTRAL ulcers, especially if started EARLY (within 48-72 hours of antibiotics).
